Background In atrial fibrillation ( AF ), a more extensively fibrotic left atrium ( LA ) provides a substrate for arrhythmias and increases risk of relapse following ablation. Fibrocytes are bone marrow–derived circulating mesenchymal progenitors that have been identified in the atrium of patients with AF who have valvular diseases. The present study investigates the associations between circulating fibrocytes and LA fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after ablation in patients with persistent AF . Methods and Results We measured the proportion, differentiation, and migration of circulating fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF (n=40), those with paroxysmal AF (n=30), and sinus rhythm controls (n=30). LA low‐voltage (fibrosis) area was identified by an electroanatomic mapping system, and patients were followed up for 1 year after ablation. The relationship between circulating fibrocyte percentage and LA low‐voltage area or recurrence was assessed by multivariate regression analysis. Circulating fibrocyte percentage positively associated with LA low‐voltage area in the persistent AF group, and circulating fibrocyte (≥4.05%) was a significant predictor of 1‐year recurrence after ablation. Cultured fibrocytes exhibited enhanced potential of differentiation in the persistent AF group (67.58±1.54%) versus the paroxysmal AF group (56.67±1.52%) and sinus rhythm controls (48.43±1.79%). Furthermore, expression of fibroblast activation markers and cell migratory ability were also elevated in differentiated fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF . Transforming growth factor β1 and stromal cell–derived factor 1 were elevated in the plasma of patients with persistent AF and were shown to promote fibrocyte differentiation and migration, respectively. Conclusions In patients with persistent AF , increased circulating fibrocytes served as a marker of LA fibrosis and recurrence. atrial fibrillation atrial fibrosis fibrocyte differentiation biomarker Subject Categories Atrial Fibrillation Fibrosis Translational Studies National Nature Science Foundation of China 81201656 81630009 81500276 81570313 Chang Jiang Scholar Program of China source-schema-version-number 2.0 component-id jah33025 cover-date 20 March 2018 details-of-publishers-convertor Converter:WILEY_ML3GV2_TO_NLMPMC version:version=5.3.4 mode:remove_FC converted:10.04.2018 ( J Am Heart Assoc . 2018 ; 7 : e008083 DOI: 10.1161/JAHA.117.008083 .) 29535140 Clinical Perspective What Is New? Circulating fibrocytes were able to predict left atrial fibrosis status and atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after first‐time ablation in patients with persistent AF. Circulating fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF exhibited a hyperactivated status and had an enhanced capacity to differentiate into myofibroblasts. Transforming growth factor β1 and stromal cell–derived factor 1 were the causative mediators that promoted fibrocyte differentiation and migration, respectively. What Are the Clinical Implications? In patients with persistent AF, circulating fibrocytes could serve as a useful cellular marker both for the degree of left atrial fibrosis and the recurrence after single ablation. Inhibiting fibrocytes during AF progression might be useful as an adjuvant treatment to improve outcomes of catheter ablation for persistent AF. Introduction Atrial fibrillation (AF) is globally the most common arrhythmia contributing significantly to mortality and morbidity. 1 Large clinical trials have shown lack of significant benefits of using antiarrhythmic medications in the treatment of AF. 2 , 3 While catheter ablation has become the routine intervention for AF, recurrence rates remain high, ranging from 30% to 60% across reports. 4 , 5 Atrial structural remodeling together with fibrosis is an important mechanism for AF persistence. A more extensively fibrotic left atrium (LA) increases the rate of relapse after ablation. 6 , 7 To date, a reliable circulating marker that can predict atrial fibrosis and recurrence following ablation is limited. Resident cardiac fibroblasts are a primary source of collagen production during both homeostatic maintenance and the development of fibrosis. In addition, recent studies have implicated fibrocytes as another important cellular source of collagen, contributing to cardiac fibrosis. 8 Fibrocytes are circulating progenitor cells and are able to migrate to sites of tissue injury where they differentiate into fibroblasts and produce extracellular matrix proteins upon stimulation. 8 Fibrocytes express hematopoietic stem cell marker CD34, leukocyte marker CD45, and a variety of mesenchymal markers, including collagen I. 8 Recruitment of fibrocytes into tissue is associated with CD34 downregulation and α‐smooth muscle actin upregulation. 9 Fibrocytes are involved in various fibrotic disorders, including asthma, systemic sclerosis, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 In addition, fibrocytes have been identified to contribute to myocardial infarction or heart failure–induced cardiac fibrosis in animal models. 14 , 15 , 16 Recently, fibrocytes were found in the atrium of patients with AF who had valvular heart diseases, 17 which prompted us to investigate the diagnostic value and functions of circulating fibrocytes in the setting of AF. In the present study, our hypothesis is that circulating fibrocytes are increased and activated in the setting of AF and could be an important indicator for LA fibrosis and AF recurrence following ablation.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF) and its associated Left Atrial (LA) fibrosis progression and recurrence.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Circulating fibrocytes, bone marrow-derived mesenchymal progenitors, are key contributors to LA fibrosis and AF recurrence in persistent AF. These fibrocytes exhibit an enhanced ability to differentiate into myofibroblasts, characterized by increased spindle-shaped cells and CD45+/collagen I+ positive cells. This differentiation and their migratory capabilities are notably increased in persistent AF patients. Differentiated fibrocytes are in a hyperactivated state, marked by elevated levels of  1-smooth muscle actin, collagen I, collagen III, and fibronectin, along with upregulated mRNA expression of CXCR4, C-C chemokine ligand 2, MMP-2, TGF 21, IL-8, and platelet-derived growth factor receptor B. Elevated plasma levels of Transforming growth factor  21 (TGF 21) and Stromal cell 1derived factor 1 (SDF1) in persistent AF patients are crucial mediators. TGF 21 promotes fibrocyte differentiation, activating Smad2/3 and stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways. SDF-1, via the SDF-1/CXCR4 axis, enhances fibrocyte migration and chemotaxis, facilitating their recruitment to affected tissues. These differentiated fibrocytes also act as a cellular source for plasma inflammatory mediators, expressing high levels of cytokines, chemokines, and MMPs, thereby enhancing inflammatory responses and contributing to atrial structural remodeling.
related_biomarkers: stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: Cultured fibrocytes from persistent AF patients exhibited enhanced differentiation potential (67.58 11.54%) compared to paroxysmal AF patients (56.67 11.52%) and sinus rhythm controls (48.43 11.79%), showing a graded effect. A circulating fibrocyte percentage of  34.05% was identified as a critical threshold. Patients with persistent AF having  34.05% circulating fibrocytes had a 100% recurrence rate (8/8) after ablation, significantly higher than the 15.6% (5/32) recurrence rate in those with <4.05% fibrocytes. For combined AF types,  34.10% was a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation. Specific concentrations of recombinant proteins were used to promote differentiation (e.g., SDF-1 100 ng/mL, TGF 21 10 ng/mL, IL-8 100 ng/mL).
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Circulating fibrocytes serve as a specific marker for Left Atrial (LA) fibrosis and recurrence, particularly in patients with persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF). They are able to predict LA fibrosis status and AF recurrence after first-time ablation in this specific population. Critically, circulating fibrocyte percentage was a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF patients (P=0.05) but was not found suitable or significant for recurrence prediction in patients with paroxysmal AF. All recurrent AF cases observed were persistent, reinforcing the specificity for persistent AF.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: The primary target population is patients with persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF) undergoing first-time catheter ablation. The study also included patients with paroxysmal AF and sinus rhythm controls. Specific exclusion criteria encompassed significant cardiac (e.g., LVEF <50%, high BNP), cerebrovascular, or other vascular diseases (except hypertension), diabetes mellitus, recent surgery/trauma, fibrotic/inflammatory diseases, cancer, and severe renal dysfunction.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Elevated circulating fibrocytes serve as a useful cellular marker for assessing the degree of Left Atrial (LA) fibrosis and for predicting recurrence after single ablation in patients with persistent AF. A high circulating fibrocyte percentage ( 34.05%) is strongly associated with LA low-voltage area (fibrosis) and is a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation. These fibrocytes contribute to AF progression and enhance inflammatory responses. Inhibiting fibrocytes during AF progression could serve as a beneficial adjuvant treatment to improve catheter ablation outcomes for persistent AF.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Circulating fibrocytes provide significant diagnostic utility for LA fibrosis assessment and act as a crucial prognostic marker for AF recurrence, classifying patients with  34.05% circulating fibrocytes as having an adverse risk for relapse. This makes them a relevant risk factor in the context of persistent AF.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: Circulating fibrocytes are identified as a reliable, useful cellular marker and strong predictor for Left Atrial (LA) fibrosis and Atrial Fibrillation (AF) recurrence in persistent AF patients, addressing a current unmet need for such markers. Specifically, a circulating fibrocyte percentage  34.05% showed a reliable association with LA low-voltage area and predicted 1-year AF recurrence after ablation in persistent AF with 62% sensitivity and 96% specificity (P=0.05). However, they are not suitable for recurrence prediction in paroxysmal AF. Limitations noted include the small group size, lack of long-term post-ablation follow-up, and unclear effects of medication.
recommended_alternatives: While no specific alternative biomarkers for measurement were recommended, the study suggests that targeting the TGF 21/TGF 2R1 or SDF-1/CXCR4 pathways could be a useful therapeutic strategy for preventing AF progression or enhancing catheter ablation outcomes.
